final_answer:
PRIVILEGED - ANTITRUST RISK ASSESSMENT AND HSR FILING STRATEGY: Crescent Fund IV / Triton Industrial Gas Distribution (record as of April 2025: SPA signed 4/14/25; HSR due 4/28/25)

1. BOTTOM LINE
- HSR filing is mandatory and substantive risk is high. A Second Request is probable. Clearance most likely requires an FTC consent decree divesting overlap branches in at least Hattiesburg, Gulfport-Biloxi and Baton Rouge, and probably New Orleans and Mobile. Branch-level FY2024 revenue for that package is roughly $60-91M against the $40M SPA cap (s.6.4(c)). The cap, the 10/31/25 outside date and the $21.25M reverse break fee are mis-sized for that outcome.
- The record is not filing-ready. Share/HHI data conflict across documents, six further overlap MSAs are unanalyzed, the HSR threshold, fee and lookback are misstated, and hot documents will be produced.
- Recommendation: file only on a reconciled data set; pre-pitch a fix-it-first remedy with an upfront buyer; decide now whether to pay for Louisiana remedies or walk at $21.25M; freeze integration; impose a gun-jumping protocol.

2. HSR MECHANICS (corrections to deal documents)
- Reportable: yes ($425M = $310M cash + $95M assumed debt + up to $20M earnout; reportable however the debt and earnout are valued). Correct 2025 figures effective 2/21/25: size-of-transaction $126.4M (the $119.5M cited is the 2024 figure); fee for $179.4M-$555.5M is $105,000, not $160,000, and the cited "$161.5M-$500M tier" does not exist in 2025 (FTC/Federal Register notice 1/22/25). SPA s.6.3(b) ("or such other amount") tolerates this; fix the IC fee authorization.
- Size-of-person is met on Triton's own numbers ($274M sales; $198M assets). Fund IV's $2.8B is uncalled commitments, not assets; the IC memo's rationale is wrong though the result is not.
- Filing person is unresolved: the prior-acquisitions summary names Crescent Capital Partners, LP as UPE; the IC memo/SPA treat Fund IV as parent and Praxion as a Fund III company. Control under 16 CFR 801.1(b) follows the right to 50% of profits/assets. If Funds III and IV are separate persons, Praxion is an "associate" (overlap still reported), and the planned Triton-into-Praxion integration needs separate HSR analysis.
- Timing: SPA s.6.3(a) requires filing by 4/28/25 (10 business days). The 30-day waiting period then ends about 5/28/25 (15 U.S.C. 18a(b); 16 CFR 803.10); a Second Request extends it to 30 days after substantial compliance. Pull-and-refile (SPA s.6.3(g); 16 CFR 803.12(c)) buys one more 30-day period without a new fee; use it only to complete a negotiated fix. Missing 4/28 breaches s.6.3 and forfeits the outside-date extension (s.8.1(e)(iii)), so get a written seller waiver if the filing slips. The 8/1/25 closing works only if no Second Request issues; the IC and board decks themselves put Second Request timelines at 6-12 months.
- Form currency: the expanded form (effective 2/10/25) governed this filing. Later, on 2/12/26, E.D. Tex. vacated the rule (Chamber of Commerce v. FTC); the Fifth Circuit denied a stay and the PNO now accepts the old form while the appeal is pending. That does not change the April 2025 posture but would govern any refiling today.

3. DISCLOSURES AND DOCUMENTS
- Prior acquisitions: the final rule's lookback is five years (not ten, as the IC memo, prior-acquisitions summary and SPA s.6.5(a)(iii) state), for both acquiring and acquired persons, limited to targets with over $10M sales/assets in overlapping NAICS codes. Delta Cylinder (3/2022) is in. Coastal Air & Gas (9/2023; Beaumont branch FY24 revenue $5.7M) likely falls below the test (check assets); disclose it anyway, since over-disclosure is cheaper than omission.
- Narrative errors to correct before filing: (a) the summary says Jackson, MS is not an overlap and Praxion had "limited prior presence," but the branch tab shows Triton's Jackson branch (TGD-024) open since 2010, so Delta was a horizontal acquisition into a Triton market; (b) the IC memo says Delta added about $12M annual revenue while the Jackson branch's FY24 revenue is $6.2M. "Independent business decisions" rebuttals sit badly with the IC memo's "systematic platform-building" language.
- Responsive "transaction-related" documents (old Items 4(c)/(d); new form equivalents): IC memo (1/22/25), Praxion synergy deck (2/10/25), Rennick 12/15/24 email, and, for Triton's filing, the 3/3/25 Garza board deck. Only counsel-directed work (Pinnacle, prior-acquisitions summary) may be withheld, with a privilege log (16 CFR 803.3(d)). Hot statements: "eliminate duplicative competitive pressure," "set market-appropriate pricing," "dominant Gulf Coast platform," consolidation will "reduce the intensity of local competition," "stop the pricing war ... lead on price," shared customers lose the ability to "play" the parties "against each other." These cannot be sanitized, only accurately contextualized. Issue a litigation hold now, prepare Rennick, Trinh, Dunleavy and Okafor for interviews, and stop creating business-side commentary on Pinnacle's findings.

4. SUBSTANTIVE RISK (Clayton Act s.7, 15 U.S.C. 18; 2023 Merger Guidelines, retained by FTC/DOJ 2/18/25)
4.1 Framework. Guideline 1 presumes illegality at post-merger HHI above 1,800 with change above 100, or share above 30% with change above 100. Pinnacle, the synergy deck and the IC memo use 2010-style cutoffs (2,500/200) and call Mobile merely "scrutiny." Under the 2023 test all five MSAs trip the HHI presumption on either dataset below. Geographic markets are local: gas delivery radius is stated as 100-150 miles (Pinnacle) versus 150-250 (IC memo, board deck), which matters for cross-state overlap (Praxion Lake Charles/Triton Beaumont).
4.2 Concentration (bulk gas; deal-document figures versus workbook revenue/market)
- Baton Rouge: 42%, +864 vs 37.8%, +662
- New Orleans: 38%, +690 vs 25.3%, +311
- Gulfport-Biloxi: 52%, +1,280 vs 42.2%, +846 (packaged 51.3%; specialty 56.2%)
- Hattiesburg: 61%, +1,848 vs 37.3%, +687 (specialty 46%)
- Mobile: 28%, +360 vs 19.7%, +191
The workbook cannot support the headline shares in the documents the agency will receive (Triton shares of 18/23/32/33/18% versus 11/15/27/19/10% from revenue/market). Stated pre-merger HHIs do not reconcile: New Orleans' listed shares cannot produce 1,980 (maximum about 1,619), and Hattiesburg's listed shares (33/28/22/17) imply at least 2,646, not 2,141. Rebuild from invoice data before any submission.
4.3 Product markets. Specialty is 34.7% in the overlap states and 56%/46% in Gulfport/Hattiesburg (workbook); it is likely a separate market (blending, ISO 17025 certification, 12-24 months to enter). Medical gas is 20.6% statewide but leaves only the merged firm and Linde in Hattiesburg and Gulfport-Biloxi, with 6-18 month licensing barriers. Data conflicts: Triton Hattiesburg (TGD-009) and Praxion Gulfport (PGS-006) show no FDA/pharmacy license yet book medical revenue and serve hospital accounts; Triton's medical summary reports 14 licensed branches and $38M medical revenue versus 9 and $20.2M in the workbook. Resolve before representing anything to staff, and because licenses drive divestiture-buyer design.
4.4 Overlap scope is understated. The branch tab flags 23 overlap-MSA branches (Praxion 11, Triton 12), not Pinnacle's 17 (missing both Slidell, both Pascagoula and both Mobile North branches). Both firms also operate in Jackson, Lafayette, Lake Charles, Houma-Thibodaux, Shreveport and Meridian (Praxion $48.9M, Triton $30.3M) - flagged "N" and absent from SPA Schedule 6.4, Pinnacle and the synergy deck. The workbook's "overlap" subtotals ($283M; 34 branches) are statewide, not MSA-level.
4.5 Customers. Twenty-two shared customers: $50.3M Praxion and $71.1M Triton spend (16.1% and 25.9% of revenue), many rated high or very high switching cost. PetroStar is $30.5M combined and Gulf Coast Shipbuilders $20.2M combined (the IC memo's "$22M/$14M combined" are Triton-only figures). The workbook, synergy deck and board deck all describe dual-sourcing as price discipline. Agencies will interview customers; contracts expiring during review include Mobile Shipbuilding (10/25), Magnolia Steel (11/25), Southern Fabricators (12/25) and PetroStar (12/26).
4.6 Defenses and limits. (a) Rivals: Air Products and Matheson have no branches in Gulfport-Biloxi or Hattiesburg (Competitor tab); Linde is the sole Hattiesburg alternative; Gulf States lacks medical/specialty; Dixie sells only welding. The IC memo's claim that Linde/Matheson constrain Mississippi is unsupported, and Pinnacle's table (Matheson 13% in Gulfport) conflicts with the workbook (5.1%; zero branches). Entry: no recent entry shown. (b) Efficiencies (2023 Guidelines s.3.3: merger-specific, verifiable, not from reduced competition): branch consolidation ($7.2M, 40%) and pricing-power statements do not qualify; procurement ($5.8M) and G&A ($5.0M) are plausible but modest, with no pass-through commitment. (c) "Unsustainable" competition and excess capacity are not defenses; Triton's 350 bp Louisiana margin erosion proves competition the merger would end. (d) Serial acquisitions (Guideline 8): Delta, Coastal and the 2019 platform buy support a cumulative-effects theory; commission Pinnacle's pre-roll-up share reconstruction.
4.7 Precedent corrections. The documents cite a "2019 Linde/Praxair" action requiring distribution divestitures in "seven MSAs." The FTC's consent was October 2018 and covered nine industrial gas markets, with production/supply assets sold to Messer and Matheson - not a distribution-branch case. The better analogue is FTC's Air Liquide/Airgas (2016), which included divesting three retail packaged welding-gas stores. Pinnacle's "2022 DOJ Midwest" clearance is uncited and unverified. Expect the FTC to review; state AGs (LA, MS, AL) may sue under Clayton Act s.16.

5. SPA ECONOMICS
- Mechanics: the cap is $40M of CY2024 revenue, counts revenue lost or impaired and behavioral restrictions (s.6.4(c)-(d)), and extends to Praxion; there is no duty to litigate (s.6.4(f)). A Burdensome Condition lets Acquiror terminate after a 30-day cure (s.8.1(d)) and pay the $21.25M fee, as does outside-date termination (s.8.2(b)); s.7.1(a) also fails on a written threat to sue. The "hell-or-high-water" label is therefore wrong (it is capped), and the fee is effectively the price of a walk option; Crescent Capital Partners guarantees it (s.10.13).
- Exposure (workbook FY24, smaller party per MSA): Hattiesburg $9.4M + Gulfport-Biloxi $16.1M = $25.5M; plus Mobile $11.6M = $37.1M; plus Baton Rouge $25.8M = $62.9M; plus New Orleans $28.5M = $91.4M, before about $30M in the six unanalyzed MSAs and before attrition. Only the Mississippi/Mobile package fits under the cap; Louisiana cannot. Pinnacle's $67-108M uses system-average branch revenue. The synergy deck's own $56-71M of revenue at closed branches also counts toward the cap if treated as a remedy.
- Pinnacle's advice to renegotiate the cap upward would increase Crescent's obligation; Crescent can already offer more voluntarily. The real decision is price of Louisiana remedies versus the $21.25M walk. Pinnacle's 4/10 draft found the cap "almost certainly inadequate" four days before signing.
- Outside date: 10/31/25, extendable once by 90 days to 1/29/26 (omitted from the IC memo). A Second Request from about 5/28/25 plus 6-12 months overruns even the extended date; amend the date and seek a timing agreement, or accept fee exposure.

6. STRATEGY AND NEXT STEPS
1. Immediately: litigation hold; single reconciled dataset across all 11 shared MSAs and five products; keep Pinnacle reports with counsel.
2. Fix filing inputs: $105,000 fee; five-year lookback; UPE; accurate overlap description; corrected Jackson narrative; customer data.
3. Do not file inaccurate materials to hit 4/28 (incomplete or false filings carry per-day penalties); obtain a seller waiver instead.
4. Early staff contact with a fix-it-first package: Hattiesburg, Gulfport-Biloxi (including Pascagoula), plus Baton Rouge/New Orleans packages as needed, with licensed medical/specialty capability and an identified upfront buyer. Divest viable stand-alone branches, not those slated for closure.
5. Suspend branch-closure and pricing-integration plans until clearance.
6. Gun-jumping (15 U.S.C. 18a; Sherman Act s.1): Rennick and Trinh built a customer-overlap analysis, Rennick chairs the integration committee, the workbook merges both firms' customer spend and contract dates, and Praxion's $18M synergy breakdown appears in Triton's 3/3 board deck. Establish a clean team, bar joint pricing/customer contact (SPA s.6.5(c)), and determine how Garza obtained Praxion's data.
7. Use pull-and-refile only for settlement timing; plan Second Request custodians (Rennick, Trinh, Dunleavy, Okafor, Castellanos, Hargrove) early.
8. Counsel-approved plans for customers with contracts expiring in review; present only procurement/G&A efficiencies; brief LA/MS/AL AGs.

7. UNRESOLVED
Which share dataset is correct; true pre-merger HHIs; UPE and Fund III/IV structure; shares in the six extra MSAs; whether Coastal meets the $10M test; medical-licensing data conflicts; the unverified DOJ Midwest matter; events after April 2025.
